checks: Nonnegative supporting slack has conditional mean zero for a source row in F, including a source point shared by several ambient facets. Thus that row stays in F. The remaining target marginal on F is precisely the outside-to-inside law, whose nonnegative mass is η(F)−ν(F). Adding its diagonal law restores equality of mass and affine moments. Jensen without that term yields the comparison only for nonnegative convex tests.

The affine graph map Ψ is onto the facet plane and fixes z, hence integer bases and the entire trace. Each nonempty own-fiber cut is its u-exposed face. Lower-dimensional faces are boundary-null and any shared ambient-facet tie carries the same single regular own normal u almost everywhere. At d=1 each endpoint has unit counting mass.

For each fixed integer base the t-map is an isometry, so the pushforward is the intrinsic fiber sum without the oblique ambient factor. The Gram matrix is block diagonal with I+aaᵀ and I, giving ambient factor √(1+|a|²), while projection onto the base has reciprocal factor on the orthogonal complement of its kernel.

Affine pullback preserves the martingale mean, the total correction and convex order. Substitution gives c_j−(v_j·u)a, Eᵀv_j and b_j−(v_j·u)b. A vanishing total linear part is a constant comparison. Positive-measure equality retains the original selector, and when every equality locus is null the ordinary closed indicators suffice.

Unique nonvertical ownership holds for almost every source as well as target by absolute continuity. Each source row remains on its original plane, so unique target ownership excludes crossing into any different facet. The reduced law has volume target and inherited cap source density.
Checked the frozen source locators against the complete imported source and verified every recorded original-source file digest.

overlap.comparison: Marked martingale existence and localization by preserved parameters are already available. The outside-to-inside correction concerns physical facet restriction, which need not be a preserved parameter.

The exposed-face support theorem contains the underlying supporting-plane localization mechanism. It does not provide the split of the full facet target or its intrinsic straightening and allocation pullback.
Fixed-normal support charts have unit own-face density there, including interval counting. They do not supply this lattice-preserving global affine reduction or its incoming correction.

The nonnegative convex-order packing criterion concerns prescribed masses and barycenters under a volume target. It does not identify the actual incoming law of a fixed physical martingale on a shared supporting facet.

readability: The statement separates the raw facet restriction, the equal-mass corrected law, and the intrinsic target. This distinction is necessary at shared faces and when testing signed convex functions.
review_method: Independent cold proof read, source and accepted-fact comparison, and exact rational recalculation.
summary: The corrected physical supporting-facet restriction has the stated exact incoming law. The affine reduction preserves the entire integer trace and the unweighted intrinsic fiber measure, and retains all cap allocation data.
